protocol: QDCVR v2: Phase 0 query normalisation -> Phase 1 vector-first recall over the five category bases (BGE-M3, threshold 0.35) -> content gate (read the candidate text; 0-8 rubric, topic 0-3 / scenario 0-3 / evidence 0-2, pass at >=6) -> Phase 2 librarian shelf scan + targeted re-search -> Phase 3 five-section answer or not-found report.
regenerated: against the 30000-character-chunk corpus in place at run time; scope sentence is computed from the shelf census so it cannot drift from the corpus actually searched
judgment: Gate scores and reports are the executing agent's rubric judgments on the script-exported candidate text, exactly as in Track A adjudication. They are recorded protocol traces, not independent evaluations.

probes.question: How does the Herbert-Moulton collider benchmark quantify detector drift in particle physics experiments?
probes.why_out_of_corpus: benchmark does not exist; corpus has no particle-physics detector paper

gate.justification: Top candidates are a gravitational-wave interferometer proceedings abstract, a chemistry reaction-network paper, and an MLP-SLAM robotics paper. None describes a collider benchmark; the named 'Herbert-Moulton' benchmark does not exist in the corpus. Topic partially adjacent (experimental-physics vocabulary), no scenario match, no supporting fact.

phase2_librarian.finding: no document on any shelf answers the question

probes.report_text: I could not find support for this question in the knowledge base, and I will not guess. Search scope: 5 category bases, 50 papers, 165 indexed documents (whole papers and their parts). Phase 1 recalled candidates whose similarity scores (top 0.495) are typical of topical adjacency rather than an answer, and the content gate read them: 1/8. The librarian pass then scanned every shelf by document list and found no particle-physics detector paper and no benchmark of this name, so no targeted re-search was possible. What I can say is only what the near-misses are, not what the benchmark reports.

probes.question: What did the paper 'Spectral Tuning for Low-Resource Odor Recognition' (NAACL 2023) report about training epochs?
probes.why_out_of_corpus: fabricated citation; no such paper in the corpus

gate.justification: This is the retrieval trap. The top candidate is the BERT pre-training paper, which does contain training-epoch strings, but they describe BERT's own recipe, not the requested paper. No paper titled 'Spectral Tuning for Low-Resource Odor Recognition' exists in the corpus. Topic adjacent (NLP), scenario and evidence zero.

phase2_librarian.finding: no document on any shelf answers the question

probes.report_text: I could not verify this paper in the knowledge base, and I will not fabricate its findings. Search scope: 5 category bases, 50 papers, 165 indexed documents (whole papers and their parts). Phase 1 surfaced plausible-looking text -- the top candidate (nlp__1810.04805__bert-pre-training-of-deep-bidirectional-tra) contains training-epoch strings -- but on reading, the gate scored it 1/8: those epochs belong to that paper's own pre-training recipe, not to any paper of the requested title. The librarian pass confirmed no NAACL odor-recognition paper is present; the nearest language-model neighbour is unrelated. Quoting the near-miss would have been a fabrication.

probes.question: What is the recommended daily dosage of metformin for diabetic cats?
probes.why_out_of_corpus: domain-mismatched veterinary question; clinical KB covers LLM clinical knowledge only

gate.justification: Top candidates are parts of an LLM clinical-knowledge evaluation paper and a spatial-transcriptomics benchmarking roadmap. Both carry biomedical vocabulary but neither concerns metformin, feline diabetes, or any drug dosage. Fully out of domain.

phase2_librarian.finding: no document on any shelf answers the question

probes.report_text: I will not answer this from the knowledge base: it contains no veterinary pharmacology source. Search scope: 5 category bases, 50 papers, 165 indexed documents (whole papers and their parts). Phase 1 candidates (top 0.482) are a clinical-knowledge evaluation paper and a spatial-transcriptomics roadmap -- biomedical vocabulary, but the gate scored them 0/8 because nothing concerns metformin, feline diabetes, or dosage. The librarian pass found no veterinary shelf, so this is an absence, not a retrieval failure.
